To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lesions in the central nervous system of the five patients with vitamin B12-deficiency consisted of disseminated demylination, that the lesions were mainly located in the posterior column and the posterior root, and that the lesions were located in the brain stem, the spinal cord, and the optic nerve.
the MRI findings of vitamin B12 deficiency are similar to those of multiple sclerosis and that the VEP findings are not specific.
in vitamin B12 deficient patients with funicular symptoms, MRI and CCT show lesions of the spinal cord, VEP, and BAEP show signs of demyelination, and CSF analysis shows signs of inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the question as to whether the findings of MRI, CT, VEP, and BAEP in vitamin B12-deficient myelopathy are similar to the findings of multiple sclerosis.
the diagnostic possibilities of MRI, CCT and electrophysiological examinations of the nervous system in patients with vitamin B12-deficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRI, CCT, and electrophysiologic measurements are not helpful for differential diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency.
MRI and CCT are not very useful in the diagnosis of funicular myeloses.
in the presence of a demyelinating disease, the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency can be established only if a vitamin B12 deficiency is present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRI and CCT are not specific for the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency and are not useful for the diagnosis of this disease.
MRI, CCT, and VEP, as well as CSF findings, can only give a hint at the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency.

MRI is the most sensitive method for the demonstration of lesions of the central nervous system in vitamin B12-deficient myelosis, whereas the most sensitive method to demonstrate lesions of the peripheral nervous system is the EMG/ENG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MRI and CCT should always be performed in the diagnostic evaluation of patients with suspected multiple sclerosis.
in patients with suspected vitamin B12 deficiency, the diagnostic process must not be limited to the measurement of vitamin B12 in serum.
in patients with funicular spinal myelosis, MRI and CCT may be normal.
